records.abstract: Magnetic gamma alumina, a magnetic adsorbent synthesized from industrial waste, aluminum dross, via a process encompassing acid leaching, calcination at 6000C and 9000C, and subsequent magnetization, was developed for the removal of aged polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics. After conversion to gamma aloxide, the alumina content exhibited an increase in purity from approximately 58% in the initial aluminum dross to roughly 78% in the resulting GA 600 and 91% in the GA 900, respectively. The magnetic gamma alumina adsorbent (MGA) demonstrated a significant surface area and substantial magnetization values of 11 emu/g for MGA 600 and 40 emu/g for MGA 900, respectively. The batch experiment involved the investigation of various parameters influencing the removal process, including pH, temperature, and the presence of ionic species. Under optimized conditions of pH 6 and 30°C, and with a contact time exceeding 4 hours, the removal efficiency achieved by MGA 600 and MGA 900 was 87% and 76%, respectively. The presence of ions such as NaCl did not influence the removal efficiency of aged PVC microplastics. The interaction mechanism between aged microplastics and MGA appeared to involve ligand-metal bonding and halogen bonding, accompanied by morphological alterations that contributed to the removal process facilitated by the external magnetic field. Therefore, the synthesized, environmentally benign magnetic adsorbent demonstrated satisfactory efficacy in the removal of aged PVC microplastics.

records.abstract: The extensive utilization of plastics in modern human society has resulted in severe environmental pollution caused by microplastics (MP/MPs). The escalating consumption of plastics has led to pervasive presence of microplastics in aquatic environments, which not only carry toxic organic matter, transport toxic chemicals, but also spread through the food chain, seriously threatening marine life and human health. Therefore, various advanced strategies have been developed for separating and degrading MPs from water. Using magnetic materials and their nanostructures for targeting, adsorbing, transporting, and degrading MPs is a promising strategy. However, a comprehensive review of MP remediation using magnetic materials and their nanostructures is currently lacking. The present work aims to fill in the gap by providing a critical review of the recent advances in MP removal/degradation using magnetic materials. The primary focus is to compare and analyze MP’s removal efficiencies of different magnetic materials, including iron/ferrite nanoparticles, magnetic nanocomposites, and micromotors, aiming to unravel the underlying roles of magnetic materials in different types of MP degradation and present the general strategies for designing them to achieve optimal performance. Finally, the review outlines the forthcoming challenges and perspectives in the development of magnetic nanomaterials for MP remediation.

records.abstract: Microplastic pollution in water systems is increasingly reported, yet mechanistic understanding based on modelling and the behaviour of filtration processes under variable hydraulic loading is limited. This study investigated microplastic removal performance of biochar and sand filters at surface area loading rates of 50.5, 101.1 and 151.5 cm·day⁻¹ using pilot-scale filtration system. Then, a two-dimensional advection-dispersion-reaction model incorporating first-order sink was calibrated to understand the dynamics of MP filtration in biochar and sand filters. The uncertainty and sensitivity were quantified using bootstrap resampling and Sobol analysis. Both biochar and sand-based filtration systems exhibited comparable removal performance, with median efficiencies of 92-96% and 90-93%, respectively. Total suspended solids removal showed weak correlation with MP number (|R| ≤ 0.63, p > 0.05), indicating the importance of direct MP monitoring. The Bayesian group-level calibration was used to understand transport regimes. Median effective length (λ) for biochar filter exceeded sand by 53-69%, attachment efficiency (α) was significantly larger in biochar filter (p ≪ 0.001) and deposition coefficients (Kd) increased with hydraulic loading (slope ≈ 6.0×10⁻⁵ per cm·day⁻¹, p ≪ 0.001). Sobol analysis identified dispersion (Dx) as the dominant source of predictive sensitivity (ST ≈ 0.76-0.79), followed by λ. The calibrated model reproduced effluent concentrations within ±10% for >90% of observations, generated design curves linking effective length to target MP removal and demonstrated biochar’s suitability as a high efficiency, space saving filtration medium compared to sand. Future research should focus on the importance of residence-time optimisation and MP polymer-specific filtration dynamic

records.abstract: Abstract Microplastic contamination of raw water used by small-scale drinking-water depots is an emerging concern, as conventional treatment is not designed to remove particles below five millimetres. This study evaluated the removal efficiency of a rice husk biochar filter for microplastics in raw water from a drinking-water depot in Aceh Besar Regency, Indonesia. A laboratory-scale acrylic column was operated under five media configurations: an unmodified control (silica sand and gravel only), a five-centimetre bed of raw, non-pyrolysed rice husk, and pyrolysed biochar beds of five, ten and fifteen centimetres. Microplastic abundance was determined by microscopic counting before and after filtration, and polymer composition by Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. The raw water contained 120 particles per litre, dominated by fragment and pellet shapes in blue, black and transparent colours. Filtration reduced this abundance to 82 particles per litre in the control (31.67% removal), 46 particles per litre with raw rice husk (61.67%), three particles per litre with the five-centimetre biochar bed (97.50%), and to non-detectable levels with the ten- and fifteen-centimetre beds (100%). Flow rate declined progressively with bed thickness, from 25.6 to 17.7 millilitres per minute, consistent with longer residence time promoting particle retention. FTIR spectra of the effluent particles retained absorption bands consistent with oxidised polyethylene or polypropylene, with indications of polystyrene, closely resembling the raw water spectrum. These findings show that an unmodified, low-cost rice husk biochar filter, without chemical activation, can achieve high and, at sufficient bed depth, complete microplastic removal, supporting its adoption at small-scale drinking-water depots.
records.title: Rice Husk Biochar Filtration for Microplastic Removal from Raw Water at a Drinking-Water Depot in Aceh Besar, Indonesia
